# New house renderings proposed in odyssey-005 (Odyssey 2.1–102)

Additional rows for the conventions.md house-renderings table.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ἦμος δ’ ἠριγένεια φάνη ῥοδοδάκτυλος Ἠώς (whole line, 2.1) | "When early-born appeared, rose-fingered Dawn," | "When early-born Dawn appeared, rose-fingered, …" | "rosy-fingered" (softens ῥόδον 'rose' into a colour), "child of morning", "early-rising", "Dawn with her rose-red fingers" |
| Ὀδυσσῆος φίλος υἱός (2.2 = 2.35, line-end) | "Odysseus' dear son" | "the dear son of Odysseus" | "Odysseus' own son", "beloved son" |
| βῆ δ’ / βῆ ῥ’ ἴμεν (2.5, 2.10) | "(he) set out to go" | "he set out for …" / "went" | "strode", "made his way" |
| θεῷ ἐναλίγκιος ἄντην (2.5) | "like to a god to look upon" | "like a god to look upon" | "godlike" (reserved for ἀντίθεος), "godlike in form" (reserved for θεοειδής), "like a god in bearing" |
| κήρυκες λιγύφθογγοι (2.6) | "the clear-voiced heralds" | "the clear-voiced heralds" | "loud-voiced", "shrill-voiced", "clear-toned" |
| κύνες ἀργοί (2.11) | "swift dogs" | "swift dogs" (+ note: 'swift' or 'white', disputed) | "white dogs", "flashing dogs", "gleaming" (reserved for γλαυκῶπις) |
| θεσπεσίην … χάριν κατέχευεν (2.12) | "wondrous … a grace poured-down" | "shed a wondrous grace upon him" | "divine grace" ("divine" reserved for θεῖος), "marvellous charm", "heavenly grace" ("heavenly" reserved for δῖος) |
| ἥρως (as title: ἥρως Αἰγύπτιος 2.15, Λαέρτῃ ἥρωι 2.99) | "the hero" | "the hero" | "lord", "warrior", "old soldier" |
| Ἴλιον εἰς ἐύπωλον (2.18) | "to Ilios of-fine-foals" | "to Ilios of the fine foals" | "of the fine horses", "horse-rich", "famed for horses" (loses πῶλος 'foal') |
| ἄγριος Κύκλωψ (2.19) | "the savage Cyclops" | "the savage Cyclops" | "wild", "brutish", "fierce" |
| δάκρυ χέων (2.24) | "a tear shedding" | "shedding tears" | "weeping" (drops χέω), "in tears" |
| ἀγορήσατο καὶ μετέειπε (2.24) | "addressed-the-assembly and spoke among them" | "addressed the assembly and spoke among them" | "harangued", "made a speech"; μετέειπε alone (2.95) = "spoke among (us/them)" |
| κέκλυτε δὴ νῦν μευ, Ἰθακήσιοι, ὅττι κεν εἴπω (whole line, 2.25) | "Hear me now, men of Ithaca, whatever I may say;" | "Hear me now, men of Ithaca, and hear what I have to say." | "Listen to me", "Ithacans, hear me", "mark what I say" |
| ὣς φάτο (2.35, 2.80) | "So he spoke" | "So he spoke" | "Thus he spoke", "So he said" (keep one form throughout) |
| πεπνυμένα μήδεα εἰδώς (of Peisenor, 2.38) | "prudent counsels knowing" | "a man versed in prudent counsels" | "wise in counsel", "shrewd" — "prudent" kept to match the table's πεπνυμένος |
| καθαπτόμενος προσέειπεν (2.39) | "accosting, he addressed him" | "addressing him directly" | "rebuked", "reproached" (the verb need not carry reproach, and does not here) |
| ὦ γέρον (2.40) | "Old man" | "Old man" | "Old sir", "Elder", "Grandfather" |
| πατὴρ δ’ ὣς ἤπιος ἦεν (2.47) | "and like a father kind he was" | "and was as gentle as a father" | "fatherly", "kind as a father to his children" |
| αἶθοψ οἶνος (αἴθοπα οἶνον, 2.57) | "the fire-faced wine" | "the wine that has the look of fire" | "sparkling", "gleaming", "fire-bright" (reserved for αἴθων), "bright wine"; built the same way as the table's οἶνοψ πόντος |
| βοῦς ἱερεύοντες καὶ ὄις καὶ πίονας αἶγας (whole line, 2.56; 2.55–58 as a block) | "slaughtering oxen and sheep and fat goats," | "slaughtering oxen and sheep and fat goats" | "sacrificing" alone (hides that this is the meal), "fatted goats" |
| ἐυκνήμιδες Ἀχαιοί (2.72) | "the well-greaved Achaeans" | "the well-greaved Achaeans" | "bronze-greaved", "armoured", "well-armed" |
| Ἀντίνοος δέ μιν οἶος ἀμειβόμενος προσέειπε (reply-formula: participle ἀμειβόμενος + προσέειπε, 2.84) | "but Antinous, him, alone, answering addressed:" | "Antinous alone spoke to him in answer:" | "answered" as a finite verb (reserved for ἠμείβετο); kept parallel to the table's ἀπαμειβόμενος προσέφη "answering addressed" |
| Τηλέμαχ’ ὑψαγόρη, μένος ἄσχετε (2.85) | "Telemachus, lofty-talker, unrestrained-in-fury" | "Telemachus, you lofty talker, unrestrained in your fury" | "braggart", "big-mouth", "high-flown", "ungovernable" — note: ὑψαγόρην also stands at 1.385 (odyssey-004), which should be checked against this |
| κέρδεα οἶδεν / εἰδώς (2.88) | "knows cunning-ways" | "knows cunning ways" | "is full of tricks", "knows all the angles", "wily" |
| κοῦροι ἐμοὶ μνηστῆρες (2.96) | "Young men, my suitors" | "Young men, my suitors" | "My young suitors", "Young lords", "Princes" |
| μοῖρ’ ὀλοή (2.100) | "the deadly fate" | "the deadly fate" | "baneful doom", "cruel fate", "destructive destiny" |
| τανηλεγὴς θάνατος (2.100) | "death that lays-at-length" | "death that lays men at length" (+ note: meaning unknown; the alternative 'bringing long sorrow' is stated) | "woeful death", "grievous death", "long-sorrowing death" (all silently choose the other ancient guess) |
| Ἀχαιϊάδες (2.101) | "the Achaean women" | "the Achaean women" | "Achaean ladies", "Greek women" |

Notes:
- Lines 2.55–58 (the suitors' feasting) and 2.93–102 (Penelope's web and her words about Laertes' shroud) are blocks that, on the drafter's knowledge of the poem, recur later nearly verbatim; they should be matched line for line to these renderings when they do.
- The Aegyptius/Telemachus exchange (2.30–32 answered by 2.42–44) is rendered with deliberately identical English, changing only persons, so the echo is audible.
- Names: Aegyptius, Antiphus, Eurynomus, Peisenor, Icarius, Laertes, Ilios — Latinized familiar forms, as the conventions do for Aegisthus.
